title: Event-triggered Implicit Perturbation for Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning of Spiking Transformers
summary: Replaces explicit read-modify-write weight perturbation with perturbation sums from dedicated hardware attached to an IMC array for zeroth-order fine-tuning of spiking networks. Compared with the simplified variant, it requires 40%-46% more silicon area and 15%-49% more energy per operation, plus custom 16 nm CMOS fabrication or synthesis. It is a circuit for SNNs, rather than software deployable on a 24 GB GPU or through a third-party API.
rationale: Circuit design for IMC spiking-network accelerators, without a conventional language-model or GPU software component the reader can adopt.
technique: Implicit zeroth-order perturbation for IMC spiking networks

claims.statement: Replaces explicit read-modify-write weight perturbation with perturbation sums from dedicated hardware attached to an IMC array for zeroth-order fine-tuning of spiking networks. Compared with the simplified variant, it requires 40%-46% more silicon area and 15%-49% more energy per operation, plus custom 16 nm CMOS fabrication or synthesis. It is a circuit for SNNs, rather than software deployable on a 24 GB GPU or through a third-party API.
IPZO reduces perturbation energy to 0.46x-0.83x of explicit weight perturbation; PGU-XOR matches software RNG accuracy, 76.41% versus 76.53% on CIFAR-10, while PGU-Reuse loses 9.56 points.

equations.headline: Perturb the output, keep the weights in place
equations.explanation: Distributivity separates the weighted input from its perturbation contribution. Their sum reconstructs the perturbed output.
equations.objective: Avoid rewriting stored weights during perturbation evaluations.
equations.evidence: Section IV-A establishes algebraic equivalence. This identity alone does not establish an energy saving.

equations.headline: Find the energy break-even point
equations.explanation: R compares implicit and explicit perturbation energy. The numerator grows with batch size B and time steps T; R below one favors IPZO.
equations.objective: Identify workloads where avoided memory operations outweigh perturbation generation.
equations.evidence: At B = 64 and T = 4, the authors report ratios of 0.83 in BIT8 and 0.46 in BIT1. Figure 15 compares post-layout IPZO simulation with estimated EPZO energy. This is perturbation energy in a 16-nm IMC design, not measured GPU inference cost.
